fields.headline: I pick at my skin when life gets *loud*, and I've been doing it a lot this week.
I can explain my compulsions better than most textbooks. Knowing all of it still hasn't made my hands *stop*.
Every compulsion is trying to get rid of a feeling. The relief is real, and it leaves almost as fast as it *came*.
Then the shame shows up, and shame is exactly the kind of feeling that sends me right *back* to it.
So I'm done yelling at myself to stop. I'm getting curious about what I'm trying to *escape* instead.
Under the picking there's usually an old belief, like I have to fix this right now or *something* bad happens.
I'm not broken for doing this. I'm a person whose brain built a way to *cope*.

fields.headline: Catch it *kindly*.
items: Name the feeling underneath in one word.
Tell yourself: it makes sense, and I can wait one breath.

fields.headline: Get *under* the urge.
fields.text: Notice when the urge shows up, name the feeling and belief underneath it, and practice meeting yourself without shame. Alongside treatment, never instead of it. There's an app for that.
